quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs harm many skills you need to drive safely. They slow your reaction time, hurt your coordination, reduce your alertness, and make it hard to concentrate.

questions.question: You must yield to children playing in the streets.
questions.explanation: You must drive carefully where children are present. Slow down near schools, playgrounds, and residential areas.

questions.question: Only ____ can lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC).
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to remove alcohol from your system. Eating, drinking coffee, or anything else cannot speed up this process.

questions.question: Which statement about backing on a roadway is true?

options.text: Signal first to warn traffic behind you that you are about to stop.
You don't need to check for traffic when backing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal first to warn traffic behind you that you are about to stop.
questions.explanation: Always look behind you to check for traffic before backing up. Only back up where it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: What should you do after an accident?

options.text: Secure the area, call authorities, and help the injured.
Report the accident the following week.
Go to the nearest store and call your insurance company.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secure the area, call authorities, and help the injured.
questions.explanation: After an accident, stop your vehicle and move it off the roadway if possible. Help anyone injured, protect the accident scene, call police right away, exchange information with other drivers, and report it to the DMV and your insurance company.

questions.question: You must stop when a school bus is unloading children on a two-lane road.
questions.explanation: You must stop for a school bus loading or unloading passengers from either direction on a two-lane road. You must also stop when approaching the bus from behind on a four-lane road.

questions.question: You cannot pass a school bus when its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: When you see a school bus with flashing red lights, stop before you reach it and stay stopped until the lights turn off. On a road with a median, vehicles on the opposite side do not have to stop.

questions.question: When in a travel lane on the roadway:

options.text: You may stop to drop off passengers.
You may stop to look up an address.
You may make a U-turn or back up if you miss a freeway exit.
Don't stop. Keep driving until you can safely pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Don't stop. Keep driving until you can safely pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane for any reason. Keep moving until you can safely pull over. If you miss your exit, do not back up. Drive to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around.

questions.question: Which of the following is against the law and can result in fines and/or jail time?
questions.explanation: Speeding is illegal. The speed limit is the maximum speed you can drive. Racing on a public road can result in fines and/or jail time.

questions.question: At an intersection with no signs or signals, you arrive at the same time as a vehicle to your right. You should:

options.text: Speed up and drive through the intersection.
Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
Drive through and force the other vehicle to stop.
Honk your horn and drive through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Yield to it and proceed only after it has safely passed.

questions.question: If you drink several beers, alcohol's effects will only go away by:
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol's effects from your body. Coffee, exercise, or cold showers do not speed this up. Your body needs about one hour to process one drink.

questions.question: When you see this yellow sign, you should:

options.text: Stop at the crosswalk until a crossing guard tells you to go.
Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if children are in the crosswalk.
questions.explanation: A five-sided sign warns you that a school is near. Watch carefully and stop if children are crossing.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: A round sign always means a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: What colors are signs that show the distance to the next highway exit?
questions.explanation: Green signs with white letters give you information about destinations.

questions.question: Before turning, you should:
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn.

questions.question: Drivers must be careful when passing large vehicles and should not drive beside them for long periods.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles have big blind spots on both sides. Do not drive next to a large vehicle for long. Move forward or fall back instead.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt, you should:

options.text: Use both the lap belt and shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap belt and shoulder belt.
questions.explanation: Wear both parts of a two-part seat belt. Using only one part does not protect you well. If you have an automatic shoulder belt, always buckle the lap belt too.

questions.question: You must stop at a railroad crossing when:

options.text: A flagger tells you to stop.
A stop sign controls the crossing.
Flashing red lights and gates are operating.

questions.explanation: Stop at a railroad crossing if a flagger signals you to stop, if there is a stop sign, or if flashing red lights and gates are operating.

questions.question: You should not stop suddenly in front of large trucks and buses because:

options.text: Small vehicle drivers cannot see large trucks and buses well in their rearview mirrors.
Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop due to their size and weight.
Large trucks and buses travel faster than small vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks and buses need longer distances to stop due to their size and weight.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles need more distance to stop than small cars. A sudden stop in front of a large vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not be able to stop in time.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?

options.text: Being alert and able to focus.

questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your nervous system. It reduces alertness and focus, increases reaction time, and greatly reduces coordination.

questions.question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Move out of the aggressive driver's way.
Stare at the driver as they pass you.
Speed up while they are passing you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: When you meet an aggressive driver, move out of their way. Do not make eye contact with them. Do not speed up—this may make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: You are driving on the freeway behind a large truck. How far back should you drive?

options.text: Closer than you would follow a regular car.
Farther back than you would follow a regular car.
To the right side of the truck and wait to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther back than you would follow a regular car.
questions.explanation: Drive farther behind a large truck than you would a regular car. Large trucks have bigger blind spots where the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: Another driver cuts you off in traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Pull next to them and yell.
Flash your high beams at them.

questions.explanation: To avoid road rage, do not take it personally if another driver cuts you off. Just let it go and keep driving safely.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get through quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: In a work zone, slow down and be ready to stop. Follow posted speed limits and watch for workers and changing conditions.

questions.question: Alcohol is the main cause of fatal car crashes.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is the top killer on roads. It hurts your vision and slows your reaction time. Even small amounts of alcohol affect your driving, even if you are not legally drunk.

questions.question: What can cause distracted driving?

options.text: Talking or texting on a phone.

questions.explanation: Drivers must make 200 decisions for every mile driven. Any task that takes your focus off driving is dangerous.

questions.question: Before you change lanes, what should you check?

options.text: Look over your shoulder for other vehicles.

questions.explanation: Check your side and rearview mirrors for traffic behind you. Then look over your shoulder to check for vehicles in your blind spot before moving.

questions.question: When parallel parking, what is the best way?

options.text: Signal right, drive past the space, stop, then back in.
Park within 18 inches of the curb.
Center your car to give other cars room to move.

questions.explanation: Signal right and stop next to the front car. Back into the space. Park within 18 inches of the curb. Center your car to leave room for other vehicles to move.

questions.question: When must you yield to a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog?

options.text: Only when the guide dog is leading them across the street.
Only if a crossing guard is present.

questions.explanation: Always give the right-of-way to pedestrians using a guide dog or white cane.

questions.question: Where is it illegal to pass another vehicle?

options.text: At a street crossing or highway intersection

questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills, curves, or where you cannot see far enough ahead. Do not pass at street crossings, railroad crossings, where signs say no passing, or where a solid yellow line is on your side. Do not pass when the car ahead has stopped for a pedestrian or in work zones where it is unsafe.
